blocks.text: Industrial chemical facilities need strict safety measures to prevent accidents and protect workers and the environment. These include:

items: Workers should use personal protective equipment (PPE) such as gloves, goggles, helmets, lab coats and protective shoes to avoid injuries from chemicals, heat or harmful fumes.

Chemicals must be properly labelled, handled and stored according to their properties. Flammable, toxic or corrosive substances should be kept in suitable containers and separate storage areas to prevent leaks, spills, contamination or dangerous reactions.

Industries should have clear emergency plans for fires, chemical spills, gas leaks or explosions. Emergency exits, fire extinguishers, first-aid kits and spill-control materials should be available, and workers should know how to respond in emergencies.
Good ventilation is needed to remove toxic gases, fumes and dust from the workplace; proper airflow reduces the risk of breathing harmful substances.

Workers must receive proper safety training on handling hazardous materials and operating equipment. Regular inspection and maintenance of machines, pipelines and storage tanks help detect faults early and reduce the risk of industrial accidents.
